items.headline: Carolina's road form is the standout number on the slate
items.body: Carolina arrive in St. Louis with the pick of the road records here: 6-1-1 away from home, 8-2-2 overall, 47 goals scored against 33 conceded and a last ten of 8-1-1 that survived an overtime defeat. The Blues are 3-0-1 at home, yet 35 goals for and 31 against is a middling profile. Back the Hurricanes on the money line at 1.67 and take anything down to our own -169.
facts: Carolina last ten 8-1-1, current run ended in overtime
St. Louis home record 3-0-1, 35 goals for, 31 against

items.headline: Pittsburgh's home record outweighs Nashville's shot suppression
items.body: Nashville have scored 23 goals in nine outings, an average of 2.56, and their road line of 1-1-2 is the weakest travelling record in this game. Pittsburgh concede too much at 38 goals against, but they are 3-1-0 at home and score 3.36 per game. At 1.80 the market is pricing the Predators far too close, so back Pittsburgh and accept anything from -165 upward.
facts: Nashville 23 goals in nine games, 2.56 per game
Pittsburgh home record 3-1-0, 3.36 goals per game

items.headline: Washington's home splits separate two teams level on points
items.body: Both clubs sit on 10 points, so the tiebreak is venue and goal difference. Washington are 4-2-0 in six home games and score 3.33 per game; Buffalo are 1-1-2 on the road and have shipped 37 goals while scoring 28. The Capitals also have 30 goals of their own against 29 conceded. There is no usable OLBG decimal on this market, so our line of -194 stands alone: back Washington at that price or better.
facts: Washington home record 4-2-0, 3.33 goals per game
Buffalo road record 1-1-2, 28 goals for, 37 against
No OLBG decimal captured for this market

items.headline: The market has overreacted to New York's road record
items.body: Ottawa's 4-2-0 home record against New York's 1-4-1 road line is the reason the visitors are available at 2.05, and it is the number we think is wrong. The Rangers have scored 37 and conceded 29; the Senators are 31 and 30. New York's last ten of 6-3-1 is also the stronger body of work. Small edge, clear direction: back the Rangers at 2.05, with -118 our line.

items.headline: Level on points, but Utah hold home ice and the goals
items.body: Fourteen points each, so this comes down to venue and scoring. Utah are 3-1-0 at home and have 41 goals on the season, 3.73 per game; Tampa Bay are 2-3-0 on the road with 34 goals and 29 conceded. The Lightning's 7-3-0 record keeps the price honest, but 1.73 on the home side is still a shade long. Our line is -119, so back Utah inside that.
facts: Utah home record 3-1-0, 41 goals, 3.73 per game
Tampa Bay road record 2-3-0, 34 goals for, 29 against
